facts.text: You play the T side on Inferno.
The bomb has not been planted; about 14 s remain on the round clock.
Your team is carrying the bomb in Arch.
One defender is visible in B site right now with an MP9.
Your team has 1 HE grenade left.
Your team is positioned: 1 in A site, 1 in Arch.
The positions of two defenders are unknown.

Keep some utility back for the post-plant
Use utility together to take space
Save, but keep one player on a last-second attempt

responses.label: Adjust the plan to the new information

debrief.whyItWorks: With limited clock, taking space with utility while the defence is unsettled is the most reliable way to plant in time. Here, 2 players faced 3 with about 14 seconds left.
debrief.cost: It spends the team's utility and options at once, leaving little for the post-plant.
debrief.assumption: The defenders cannot rotate enough players to the site before the plant.
debrief.breaksWhen: The defence stacks the chosen site and has its own utility ready for the execute.

evidenceReview.explanation: The utility left sets how much of the plan can be forced rather than hoped for. Here the team held 1 utility item.
The round clock bounds how long any plan can take. Here the round clock stood near 14 seconds.
The head count sets how many duels the team can lose and still carry out its plan. Here it was 2 against 3.

debrief.followupReview: The proposed best answer to the new information was: Adjust the plan to the new information. Reasoning: the state of the bomb has changed, which changes what the plan is for.
debrief.strongestAlternative: The closest alternative was to save the weapons, conceding the round to keep the economy intact.

counterfactual.changedFact: The defenders are known to have stacked the target site.
counterfactual.effect: The execute meets a full defence, and taking information or faking becomes stronger.
